summary.text: 女 is a whole-figure pictograph of a woman, used with the meanings “woman” and “female.” Early forms are interpreted as kneeling or seated figures; accounts differ on the position of the hands.

formation.text: Pictographic: the graph depicts a woman as a whole figure. Early forms are interpreted as kneeling or seated, with hands described as crossed or engaged in an activity.

components.text: The whole graph depicts a woman. Early forms are interpreted as a kneeling or seated figure; accounts describe the hands as crossed or engaged in an activity. It is not divided into smaller parts.

history.text: Oracle-bone and bronze forms are described as a kneeling or seated woman. Later bronze forms simplify the seated posture, and one account says the depiction had become difficult to recognize by the Warring States period. These are changes in written form, not evidence of a change in meaning.

One account proposes that the modern form is reversed relative to oracle-bone forms and interprets strokes as representing a breast. This proposed graphic analysis is not confirmed by the other cited accounts.

uncertainties.text: Accounts differ on the early figure’s posture and hand position. The proposed reversal and breast interpretation of the modern form are not confirmed by the other cited accounts.
Early inscription accounts report uses of 女 beyond “woman,” but the available dates and contexts do not establish whether each is a borrowed spelling for another word or a development in meaning.

senses.text: Early inscription accounts report female-related uses, and the Han-period Shuowen glosses 女 as “woman.” The cited inscription examples are not precisely dated here, so this is the earliest documented sense in these accounts, not proof of the graph’s original meaning or priority among early uses.
Early inscription accounts report 女 used for 母, including cited oracle-bone examples. This documents an early use or overlap, but does not establish a semantic development from “woman.”

senses.text: Inscription accounts report these uses of the graph. Some may be spellings borrowed for other words, but the available accounts do not provide enough context or sound evidence to explain each use.

A separate lexical reading is recorded with the meaning “give as a wife.” The supplied historical readings distinguish it from 女 “female,” but do not date this use or establish how the meanings are related.
Dictionary and definition records list these meanings, but do not establish when they arose or how they developed from “woman.”

limitations.text: The reported uses and dictionary glosses do not establish dated transitions among these meanings, so no semantic-development links are asserted.
